text: When an excess of aqueous sodium hydroxide, NaOH, is added to 100 cm of aqueous
For
copper(II) sulfate, CuSO , a precipitate of copper(II) hydroxide, Cu(OH) , is produced.
Examiner’s
Use
The stoichiometric equation for this reaction is,
CuSO (aq) + 2NaOH (aq) Cu(OH) (s) + Na SO (aq)
The following information gives some of the hazards associated with these reactants.
Copper(II) sulfate (solid hydrated copper(II) sulfate CuSO .5H O)
Harmful. Dangerous for the environment.
Harmful if swallowed. Irritating to eyes and skin.
Solutions of concentrations equal to or greater than 1 mol dm should be labelled HARMFUL.
Sodium hydroxide (solid NaOH)
Corrosive. Solutions of concentrations equal to or greater than 0.5 mol dm are CORROSIVE.
Solutions of concentrations equal to or greater than 0.05 mol dm but less than 0.5 mol dm
are IRRITANT.
You are to plan an experiment to investigate the molar ratio of the equation above and confirm
that it remains unchanged as the concentration of the copper(II) sulfate changes.

text: The variation of the volume with temperature of a fixed mass of an ideal gas at constant
For
pressure may be represented by a relationship known as Charles’s law,
Examiner’s
Use
V = kT
where V is the volume of a gas, T is the temperature in Kelvin and k is a constant.
An experiment was carried out to attempt to verify this law.
• A specially adapted gas syringe was filled with a sample of gas. The syringe was placed
in a temperature controlled chamber at 25 °C and left for 5 minutes. The initial volume of
gas at this temperature was 26.0 cm .
• The temperature was adjusted and, after leaving for 5 minutes, the change in gas
volume for the new temperature was recorded.
• The experiment was repeated several times at different temperatures and the results
recorded.
